facts.source: Akai MPC3000 service manual parts list (marking uPD70236GD-16); MAME src/mame/akai/mpc3000.cpp (device V53A)
facts.value: NEC uPD70236 (V53): 8086-compatible core with on-chip DMA controller, timers, interrupt controller and serial port

facts.source: MAME driver (32 MHz crystal, CLKOUT = crystal / 2); NEC 16-bit V-Series data book; Akai specifications quote a 16 MHz V53
facts.value: 32.000 MHz crystal; the CPU core runs at half of it, 16 MHz
20-bit 8086 addressing extended to 24 bits through a 64-entry page-register table (see findings/address-model.md)

facts.source: Akai MPC3000 service manual parts list; MAME driver ROM_SKIP(1) interleave
facts.value: Two AM27C020 EPROMs (IC13 = LS/even bytes, IC14 = MS/odd bytes); 512 KiB when interleaved

facts.source: MAME driver memory map; service manual parts list (IC15, IC16)

facts.value: Battery-backed RAM window at 24-bit 0x500000-0x500FFF, reached by the OS through page 61

facts.source: MAME driver comment and service parts list name the chip; nobody here has confirmed it is the device decoded at that window
facts.value: LC3517 (2K x 8 static RAM with battery)

facts.source: MAME driver; service manual parts list
facts.value: NEC uPD78C10AGQ at 12 MHz with its own 32 KiB EPROM (IC602); talks to the main CPU over a serial link

facts.source: MAME driver header and devices/sound/l7a1045_l6028_dsp_a.cpp; service manual parts list (IC28)
facts.value: L7A1045 L6028 DSP-A, 33.8688 MHz; 16-bit sample bus with 24 address bits (32 MiB sample space) separate from the CPU bus

facts.source: MAME driver I/O map; service manual parts list
facts.value: LC7981 LCD controller (modelled as an HD61830 in MAME); I/O port 0x00E0 data, 0x00E2 control/status
uPD72069, I/O ports 0x00E8-0x00EB, DMA channel 1, interrupt shared with SCSI on IRQ3
Fujitsu MB89352, I/O ports 0x00A0-0x00BF, DMA channel 0

facts.source: MAME driver header comment and I/O map
facts.value: TE7774 quad UART, I/O ports 0x00C0-0x00DF: MIDI IN 1-2, MIDI OUT 1-4, and the receive side of the front-panel link

facts.source: String at linear file offset 0x7B00F in mpc3000-vailixi-3.50; findings/interrupt-vectors.md
facts.value: The OS runs on the KADAK AMX real-time kernel (a 1983 KADAK copyright string sits in the EPROM)
Segmented 8086 code. Application routines are far cdecl: arguments pushed right to left, first argument at [BP+6], caller cleans the stack, RETF
At power-on the ROM loads the first *.SYS file on a floppy as a DOS MZ executable into RAM and jumps to it. No EPROM change is needed to run your own code

findings.summary: The five address forms used in this repository, how the V53 page registers turn a 20-bit address into a 24-bit one, and the three page tables the firmware loads.
findings.title: How addresses work on the MPC3000 (V53 extended addressing)

sources: MAME devices/video/hd61830 (register numbering used for comparison)
findings.summary: The BIOS in the top 32 KiB of the EPROM offers services through software interrupts. INT 43h writes text to the LCD, INT 41h reads files, INT 45h loads an MZ program.
findings.title: BIOS software-interrupt services (LCD text, files, program load)

findings.summary: Step-by-step route for running your own code on an MPC3000 from a floppy .SYS file, with a working minimal program, the rules it must obey, and how to test before touching a machine.
findings.title: Recipe: build and run your own program from floppy

findings.summary: OS application code is far cdecl (arguments pushed right to left, first argument at [BP+6], caller cleans up, RETF). The AMX kernel and the BIOS each use a different convention.
findings.title: Calling conventions used by the OS, kernel and BIOS

findings.summary: Common 8086 disassemblers mis-decode the V53 instructions BRKXA and RETXA and lose the instruction stream after them. Other traps are decoding one chip file alone and trusting raw opcode counts.
findings.title: Disassembler pitfalls on V53 firmware

findings.summary: The OS is two interleaved 256 KiB EPROMs. This gives the layout of the interleaved image, the reset path, and the rule that an image is identified by hash, never by the version it prints.
findings.title: MPC3000 OS EPROM layout and how to identify an image

findings.summary: At power-on every examined EPROM OS loads the first *.SYS file on a floppy as a DOS MZ executable into RAM and jumps to it. This is the only ROM path that runs code from removable media.
findings.title: The ROM floppy loader that runs a .SYS file at power-on

findings.summary: The chips on the MPC3000 CPU board and what each one does, taken from the Akai service parts list and the MAME driver.
findings.title: MPC3000 hardware overview

findings.summary: Which code owns each interrupt vector once the OS has started, who installs it, and how to install a handler the way the OS does.
findings.title: Interrupt vector table after boot

findings.summary: Where ROM, RAM, NVRAM and every peripheral sit, and which interrupt and DMA line each device uses, as modelled by the MAME driver.
findings.title: MPC3000 memory map, I/O ports, interrupts and DMA

findings.summary: On 3.12 and Vailixi 3.50 EPROMs stock OS 3.16 lets sequence data overwrite its own code and hangs at Song. With a SCSI disk its partition reader wraps the stack. Both causes and working fixes are described.
findings.title: Two memory defects in stock OS 3.16, and their fixes

findings.summary: Append a code segment to M3K316.SYS, extend its relocation table, move the new code above 3.16 at load time, and hook 3.16 by far jumps. Builds made this way run on real hardware.
findings.title: Recipe: add code to OS 3.16 and load it from floppy

findings.summary: OS 3.16 is a self-contained MZ program with its own BIOS and AMX kernel. This gives its layout, address forms, start-up, tasks, memory use and a map of 111 named routines and data objects.
findings.title: OS 3.16 (M3K316.SYS) structure, memory and named routines

findings.summary: Two blocks totalling 147,372 bytes of the 512 KiB image are empty and are not mapped by any of the firmware's page tables. Using them needs a page-table change; a smaller empty block inside the OS code range is directly reachable.
findings.title: Unused space in the OS EPROMs

firmware.label: OS 3.08 (EPROM pair)
firmware.notes: Not in the MAME ROM set. Loads .SYS files at segment 7000.
firmware.obtain: Read the two OS EPROMs (IC13 = LS, IC14 = MS, AM27C020) of a machine you own with an EPROM programmer.
firmware.source: Computed from a dump of the chips; part CRC32/SHA-1 equal the MAME mpc3000 ROM set where MAME lists the image.

firmware.notes: Hashes from MAME only. No contributor has analysed this image: no finding applies to it.
firmware.obtain: Read the two OS EPROMs (IC13 = LS, IC14 = MS, AM27C020) of a machine you own with an EPROM programmer.

firmware.obtain: Read the two OS EPROMs (IC13 = LS, IC14 = MS, AM27C020) of a machine you own with an EPROM programmer.
firmware.source: Computed from a dump of the chips; part CRC32/SHA-1 equal the MAME mpc3000 ROM set where MAME lists the image.

firmware.label: OS 3.12 (EPROM pair)
firmware.notes: MAME's default BIOS. Loads .SYS files at segment 6900.
firmware.obtain: Read the two OS EPROMs (IC13 = LS, IC14 = MS, AM27C020) of a machine you own with an EPROM programmer.
firmware.source: Computed from a dump of the chips; part CRC32/SHA-1 equal the MAME mpc3000 ROM set where MAME lists the image.

firmware.label: Vailixi OS 3.50, reference dump (EPROM pair)
firmware.notes: The dump in the MAME ROM set (BIOS banner dated 21/08/07). Units running an OS that calls itself 3.50 do not all hold these bytes: see findings/eprom-layout.md. Identify by hash, never by the version on screen.
firmware.obtain: A third-party operating system supplied by its author on EPROMs. Read the EPROMs of a machine you own.
firmware.source: Computed from a dump of the chips; part CRC32/SHA-1 equal the MAME mpc3000 ROM set where MAME lists the image.

firmware.label: OS 3.16 maintenance upgrade (M3K316.SYS, floppy-loaded)
firmware.notes: A DOS MZ executable loaded into RAM from floppy at power-on; not an EPROM image. Gone at power-off. File offsets for this id are offsets into the .SYS file itself (the load image starts at 7A00h). See findings/os316-structure.md.
firmware.obtain: Released in 2005 by its author as a floppy upgrade for the MPC3000 and MPC3000LE. Obtain the file from a source you trust and check the hash.

firmware.label: Front-panel MCU program v1.0 (uPD78C10, AM27C256, IC602)
firmware.notes: 32 KiB. No contributor has analysed this image: the panel protocol is an open question.
firmware.obtain: Read the AM27C256 at IC602 on the panel board of a machine you own.

machines.name: Akai MPC3000

questions.summary: A program loaded from floppy shares RAM with BIOS services it calls, but the full set of BIOS variables is not mapped.
questions.title: What RAM the BIOS uses

questions.summary: The byte layout of the files the MPC3000 saves and loads is not documented here.
questions.title: Disk file formats (SND, PGM, APS, SEQ, ALL, PAR)

questions.summary: DMA channel 2 is wired to IC31, whose function is not identified.
questions.title: What is on DMA channel 2

questions.summary: The BIOS writes ports C010h and C011h around interrupts. They are believed to be the on-chip interrupt controller, but this has not been confirmed.
questions.title: Ports C010h and C011h

questions.summary: The text path to the LCD is known. The controller command set as wired on this board, the graphic mode, and four of the eight INT 43h functions are not.
questions.title: LCD controller commands and graphics

questions.summary: Where MIDI bytes are received, parsed and sent inside the OS is not documented.
questions.title: MIDI handling

questions.summary: The battery-backed memory behind page 61 holds settings, but its layout, checksum and the consequences of writing it are unknown.
questions.title: NVRAM layout and what a RAM program may do to it

questions.summary: OS 3.10 is listed in the MAME ROM set but no contributor has had the image, so no finding applies to it.
questions.title: OS 3.10 has not been examined

questions.summary: Stock and modified OS 3.16 have run on hardware only on a machine with a Vailixi 3.50 EPROM. The other EPROM versions, and the load-segment move, are emulator results.
questions.title: OS 3.16 builds on real 3.08, 3.11 and 3.12 EPROMs

questions.summary: OS 3.16's structure, start-up and 111 routines are mapped. Its sequencer, MIDI, most disk code, the Mixer and five of its eight tasks are not.
questions.title: Unmapped areas of OS 3.16

questions.summary: Two places in the OS can write an I/O port taken from a table and might therefore change a page register while the OS runs.
questions.title: Page-register writes at run time

questions.summary: Address decoding on the CPU board is done by PAL devices whose equations have not been read.
questions.title: PAL address decode

questions.summary: How the panel microcontroller reports pads, keys and the wheel to the main CPU, and what the main CPU sends back, is not documented.
questions.title: Front-panel protocol (pads, keys, data wheel)

questions.summary: A floppy program can place a patched copy of the EPROM OS in RAM and restart it. This has been shown in the emulator for one image only; the details for the stock images are missing.
questions.title: Running a patched copy of a stock EPROM OS from RAM

questions.summary: The floppy loader has run from a 1.44M image on a drive emulator. Real drives and the two smaller formats have not been tried.
questions.title: Real floppy drives, and 720K / 800K disks

questions.summary: How the OS drives the L7A1045 sample DSP (voice allocation, register writes, sample memory layout, recording) is not documented.
questions.title: Sample engine and DSP registers

questions.summary: How sequences, tracks and events are stored in memory, and how the timing interrupt plays them, is not documented.
questions.title: Sequencer data model and timing

questions.summary: Most code-level findings were established on the Vailixi 3.50 reference image. The same facts are needed for the Akai images most machines carry.
questions.title: A code map for the stock OS images (3.08, 3.11, 3.12)

machines.summary: Hardware, addressing, boot path and the floppy route for running your own code are documented. The operating system's internals (sequencer, sampling, MIDI, file formats, front-panel protocol) are not.
